ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, a semicircle $O$ with diameter $BC$ intersects $AB$, $AC$ at points $D$, $E$, respectively. Segments $OD$, $OE$ are connected. If $\angle A=\alpha$, what is the measure of $\angle DOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, connect CD,\\
$\because$BC is the diameter of semicircle O,\\
$\therefore \angle BDC=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle A=\alpha$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACD=90^\circ-\angle A=90^\circ-\alpha$,\\
$\because \angle ACD$ and $\angle DOE$ are the inscribed angle and the central angle of arc $\overset{\frown}{DE}$, respectively,\\
$\therefore \angle DOE=2\angle ACD=180^\circ-2\alpha$,\\
Therefore, $\angle DOE=\boxed{180^\circ-2\alpha}$.

method.method_draft: Use the external secant angle theorem. From the image, view A as an exterior point to the semicircle, with two secants A-D-B and A-E-C cutting the semicircle; D and E are the nearer intersection points and B and C are the farther intersection points. From the text, ∠DAE = ∠BAC = α and BC is the diameter of the semicircle, so the arc BC of the semicircle measures 180°. For two secants from an exterior point, the exterior angle equals half the difference of the intercepted arcs: α = 1/2(m arc BC − m arc DE). Therefore m arc DE = 180° − 2α. Since ∠DOE is the central angle subtending arc DE, ∠DOE = 180° − 2α.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, a semicircle $O$ with diameter $BC$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. Segments $OD$ and $OE$ are connected. If $\angle A=\alpha$, what is the measure of $\angle DOE$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, connect $CD$.\\ $\because$ $BC$ is the diameter of semicircle $O$,\\ $\therefore \angle BDC=90^\circ$,\\ $\because \angle A=\alpha$,\\ $\therefore \angle ACD=90^\circ-\angle A=90^\circ-\alpha$,\\ $\because \angle ACD$ and $\angle DOE$ are the inscribed angle and the central angle of arc $\overset{\frown}{DE}$, respectively,\\ $\therefore \angle DOE=2\angle ACD=180^\circ-2\alpha$.\\ Therefore, $\angle DOE=\boxed{180^\circ-2\alpha}$.

First describe the image: In the figure there is triangle ABC, B and C are at the two ends of the horizontal base, and A is above; an upper semicircle is drawn with BC as diameter, O is located on BC and is the center of the circle; the semicircle intersects AB at D and intersects AC at E; OD and OE are connected in the figure, and what is required is the central angle ∠DOE.

Then reason: According to the method, draw auxiliary chord CD. Because BC is the diameter of the semicircle and D is on the circle, by Thales' theorem ∠BDC = 90° is obtained. Also because D is on AB and A, D, B are collinear, DC is also perpendicular to AD, that is, ∠ADC = 90°. In triangle ACD, ∠DAC is exactly the vertex angle ∠A = α of triangle ABC, therefore ∠ACD = 90° − α. Because E is on AC, CE and CA are the same straight line, so ∠ECD = ∠ACD = 90° − α. ∠ECD is the inscribed angle subtending arc DE, while ∠DOE is the central angle of the same arc DE, so ∠DOE = 2∠ECD = 2(90° − α) = 180° − 2α.
